\[
Y = 0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B,
\quad
C_b = 128 + \frac{B - Y}{1.772},
\quad
C_r = 128 + \frac{R - Y}{1.402}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(Y\): Luma
- \(C_b, C_r\): The blue and red color differences, centered at 128

These are the luma and color differences of ITU-R BT.601, as JPEG uses them. Cb and Cr are smoothed with the median or the Gaussian, and Y is kept. R, G and B come back from the exact inverse. It is R = Y + 1.402 (Cr - 128), B = Y + 1.772 (Cb - 128) and G = (Y - 0.299 R - 0.114 B) / 0.587. The eye sees fine detail mostly in brightness, which is why JPEG may store Cb and Cr at a lower resolution. So smoothing them removes color noise and keeps the detail. The combination is PixelNexus's own. The median works on whole levels, so Cb and Cr are rounded for it.
